Published online:
September 3, 2026

Geographic focus:
Europe (EU/Eurozone), with secondary focus on US

Temporal focus:
T1. Historical report [YES] — recaps recent 3-session losing streak, bond selloff, Iran war escalation
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — ECB rate hike next week, Friday NFP report, oil price trajectory, inflation persistence
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — ECB projected to deliver two additional hikes by mid-2027, luxury sector recovery outlook, persistent high rates environment

Synopsis:
European equities rebounded modestly (+0.5% STOXX 600) after a three-session selloff, as bond yields pulled back from multi-year highs. The key macro backdrop remains hawkish: elevated oil prices (above $95/bbl) tied to ongoing Iran war escalation are keeping inflation fears alive and central banks on a tightening path. The ECB is near-certain to hike to 2.5% next week with further hikes priced through mid-2027. On the US side, Chair Kevin Warsh's recent hawkish rhetoric has already shifted Fed rate hike expectations higher, with Friday's NFP the next key catalyst. Stock-specific movers include Soitec (+10.3%), WPP and Publicis (media account win), while luxury names sold off broadly. Commerzbank and Deutsche Telekom were positive outliers.
